audit: M6 campaign reproducibility and validity audit (independent exercise, Agent I3)
auditor: independent read-only research/reproducibility reviewer; no repository file modified
subject: benchmark/runs/20261008T203656Z-m6-campaign (freeze block 1, declaration commit 4481e26, integration tip 69ad4d8)
method: all artifacts read through git objects; the integration branch extracted to a temporary directory outside the repository for execution

findings.title: Gateway identity is runner-attested and the run happened on a feature worktree, not the integration tip
findings.reproduction: git show feature/aegisgraph-industrial-research:benchmark/runs/20261008T203656Z-m6-campaign/manifest.json -> code.branch='feat/m6-campaign', code.commit_source='git-rev-parse-HEAD', dataset.root='...\.worktrees\agent-m6\...', defense.version.build.commit='unknown'; git diff --stat 818cf1f 4481e26 -> 'docs/evidence/m6-freeze.md | 25 +++---' only
findings.impact: The freeze requires the gateway commit to be the integration tip; the manifest names a feature worktree branch, and the service's own build commit is 'unknown', so the code identity rests solely on the runner's git rev-parse. Benign: the freeze-declaration commit 4481e26 is docs-only (verified: it changes only docs/evidence/m6-freeze.md), so the code tree under test equals the integration tip's code at declaration. The freeze block and report do not state this.
findings.required_correction: Record in the freeze/report that the declaration commit is docs-only and that the gateway identity is runner-attested (the service does not self-report its commit).

findings.title: C6 blocked-cell enabling command is not runnable and its 'fails closed' claim is false
findings.reproduction: python scripts/bench_run.py --defense-url http://127.0.0.1:1 --model ollama:qwen3:8b --splits development,validation --config-slug probe -> 'run failed: unknown model adapter 'ollama:qwen3:8b'; available: scripted, ollama'
findings.impact: The report's C6 command uses '--model ollama:qwen3:8b' against the native runner, which accepts only 'scripted' or 'ollama'. It therefore raises RunError (unknown adapter), not the claimed fail-closed ModelUnavailable ('the adapter is declared and fails closed with this command until a model exists'). The correct native argument is '--model ollama' (UnavailableModelAdapter). The same wrong syntax appears in freeze §4 for the native runner. The legacy-kit form 'eval public --model ollama:<tag>' IS correct (verified: sentinel/cli.py accepts 'mock | ollama:<tag> | qwen3-8b | path').
findings.required_correction: Change the C6 native command to '--model ollama' and delete/correct the parenthetical; keep 'ollama:qwen3:8b' only for the legacy kit. Fix freeze §4 likewise.

findings.title: The ledger does not register the M6 campaign; P66 is stale
findings.reproduction: git show 69ad4d8:docs/evidence/ledger.md | grep -n '^| P66' -> 'pending — declared, not yet exercised'; grep for 'b6951afb' / '20261008T203656Z' -> no row
findings.impact: P66 still reads 'pending — declared, not yet exercised' and P21 still calls 8d79f032 the 'current published reference', although the campaign ran, is committed (f3129d0/df0d0f1), and established digest b6951afb with the documented delta. No ledger row records C1/C2/C3/C4, the digest, the delta, or the C3 recheck. Nothing is promoted without an artifact (all verified rows cite one), but the campaign is absent from the ledger.
findings.required_correction: Update P66 to exercised with the run directory/commit, and add a row for the campaign result (C1 digest b6951afb, C2 licence, C3 8669aadb recheck, C4 determinism, delta null) with its artifact, command and commit.

findings.title: Credential scope set and trust ceiling are asserted but not recorded in any committed artifact
findings.reproduction: git show <branch>:.../manifest.json | python -c "json.load(sys.stdin)['auth']" -> only {header, mode, principal, principal_source, scheme}; no scopes/trust_ceiling field
findings.impact: The report asserts 'scopes decision:submit (no policy:context_override)' and 'the credential's ceiling is trusted_internal'. These are consistent with code defaults (backend/aegisgraph/auth.py ROLE_SCOPES['decision_client']={decision:submit}; settings.DEFAULT_TRUST_CEILING=TrustedLevel.TRUSTED_INTERNAL; scripts/dev_issuer.py mints the same) and with the absence of any 403 in the run, but the specific values are not evidenced in the committed bytes, so the H3-04 unreachability argument ('holds no policy:context_override') rests on an unrecorded credential property.
findings.required_correction: Record the resolved scope set and trust ceiling in the run manifest's auth block (and, for H3-04, the effective policy identity reported by the gateway) so the unreachability explanation is reproducible from the artifact.

findings.title: Ledger row P43 (I2-14) states a code fact that no longer holds at the audited tip
findings.reproduction: grep -n 'IDENTITY_KEYS' benchmark/scoring.py; python -c "...json.load(score.json); swap code_commit; _report_digest -> 8d79f032..." (the digest includes code_commit)
findings.impact: P43 remains 'pending' and its cited 'code fact' is '`_decision_projection` pops `configuration`'. At the audited tip the projection replaces configuration with IDENTITY_KEYS, so the digest DOES include code_commit/dataset/policy/model/seed/splits — exactly what the campaign report §7 cites '(I2-14)' for. The report's statement is true; the ledger row is stale relative to the code it cites.
findings.required_correction: Close/rewrite P43 to the current behaviour (identity keys in the digest; the card/docstring update is the remaining acceptance item, if any).

findings.title: Freeze §8 artifact-hash list mixes raw-byte and CRLF-normalised conventions
findings.reproduction: python -c "hashlib.sha256(open(f,'rb').read()) vs .replace(b'\r\n',b'\n')" for the run dir: score.json raw=05f22292 (matches §8) but README.md raw=ca8d2139 while §8 records 94b8aed = its CRLF-normalised value; C3 artifact §8 records raw 2af5e847 (its normalised value is 6c04cb5f)
findings.impact: All recorded hashes reproduce, but score.json (CRLF file) is listed raw while README.md (CRLF file) is listed normalised, and the C3 artifact raw. The list does not say which convention applies to which file, so a reviewer cannot know whether a mismatch is real. No correctness defect.
findings.required_correction: State per-row which convention applies, or record both raw and content-sha256-lf for the two CRLF files.

summary.scope: Read-only audit of the M6 campaign against freeze block 1 at integration tip 69ad4d8 (campaign artifacts unchanged since df0d0f1). All artifacts accessed through git objects (git show / git archive); the integration branch was extracted to a temporary directory outside the repository for execution; the repository working tree was not modified (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no is empty).
methods: Byte-for-byte re-score with the committed scorer and cmp against the committed score.json.

Independent reimplementation of the metric definitions (reached set from control attack_success, ITT ASR, benign task success, decision-level and scenario-level FBR, escalation rate, licence fields) directly from outcomes.jsonl and control.jsonl.
Synthetic probe outcomes (written outside the repo) driving benchmark.scoring.score to exercise the ITT error rule and the empty-licence void rule.
Per-scenario verdict/judged-outcome/reason-code diff between the M6 run and the committed M2 reference run.
Digest recomputation with only code_commit swapped to prove the delta is commit-identity only.
Dataset key walk and grep for trust_level values; code reading of access.py/auth.py/settings.py/wire.py/runner.py for the ceiling and override paths.
Legacy digest and metric-key comparison across the M0/M1/M6 rechecks and the committed mock scorecard.
Hash verification of every recorded artifact under the declared content-sha256-lf convention (plus raw where they differ).
Execution of the C6 enabling command to observe its real failure mode; inspection of the legacy kit CLI for the C5/C7 commands.
not_covered: No real-model run exists to audit: C5 (Qwen3-8B) and C6 (native real model) are blocked, so no model-behaviour claim could be tested, and none is made.
The sealed holdout was not opened and was not decrypted; no holdout claim was checked or could be checked.

The live gateway was not re-run: the C1/C2 outcomes were not regenerated against a fresh service, only re-scored from the committed bytes (no model, and reproducing the durable-PostgreSQL run was out of scope).

The committed credential (JWT) and the run's receipt store contents were not available, so the scope set, trust ceiling and reported policy identity could not be read from the gateway side (see I3-04).
The legacy mock suite was not re-run against a live service; the C3 comparison is between committed artifacts only.
Latency numbers were not re-measured; they are host-dependent and excluded from the digest.
summary.residual_risk_statement: Every headline number and digest in the M6 campaign report is independently reproduced from the committed bytes, and the delta is exactly the reported null result with the digest moved only by code_commit; the C3 recheck is byte-identical to M0/M1 and its README table is accurate. The residual risk is not in the measurements but in their provenance: the gateway commit is runner-attested (the service self-reports 'unknown'), the credential's scopes and ceiling are asserted rather than recorded, and the evidence ledger was not updated for the campaign (P66 still 'not yet exercised', no campaign row). One blocked-cell command (C6) is not runnable as written and its fail-closed claim is false. None of these changes the measured conclusions; they are documentation/identity gaps that should be closed before the campaign is cited as a frozen result. The H3-01/H3-04 unreachability explanation is supported by the dataset and code (all declared trust_level values are at or below the ceiling; no override scope is exercised), but the 'why' rests partly on configuration facts that the artifacts do not carry — so the null result is correctly described as a limitation of the measurement.
